name: Fullstack App | Paris 2024
tagline: Fullstack e-ticket platform handling authentication, payments, and secure user flows in production-like conditions.

keyPoints: Designed to handle secure payment flows and user state consistency across sessions
Complete authentication flow (signup, email verification, password reset). Role-based access (RBAC), dashboard admin.
Purchase flow with cart persistence and merge on login. Stripe integration for secure payments.
PostgreSQL database with indexation and query optimisation.
Sensitive data encryption, controlled API access, rate limiting / load balancing.

popTagline: Developed to explore authentication, payment flows, and end-to-end application architecture in a full-stack context.

overview.mainContent: Paris 2024 is a full-stack online ticketing application for the 2024 Olympic Games, built as a study project. Visitors buy their tickets online and receive them by email as QR codes, replacing fraud-prone physical tickets.
keyPoints: Offers, cart and authentication, with the cart kept across sessions and merged on login.
Stripe payments, then e-tickets: a user key and a ticket key, concatenated into a QR code sent by email.
Admin panel to manage offers and view sales statistics.
Scheduled jobs for expired token cleanup and account deletion.
Nx monorepo: Angular client, NestJS server and shared libraries.
overview.after: It served both as a functional product and as a way to work end-to-end on a complete system: data ingestion, backend logic, API design, frontend consumption, and deployment. Even without external users, the system was operated as if failures mattered.

purpose.title: Purpose
keyPoints: To design and implement a complete full-stack application from scratch.
To practice clean separation between backend responsibilities and frontend concerns.
To implement essential security measures (SQL injection prevention, sensitive data encryption).
purpose.after: Beyond functionality, the project emphasized coherence across layers: each part of the system should remain understandable in isolation.

constraints.title: Constraints
keyPoints: Clear contract between frontend and backend: predictable APIs over ad-hoc coupling.
Reasonable scope: focus on core features rather than exhaustive coverage.
Maintainability: code that remains readable and modifiable as requirements evolve.
Production mindset: even as a study project, deployment and reliability mattered

choices.title: Business rules on the server
keyPoints: Validating carts and orders.
Handling payments and issuing tickets.
Enforcing access rules (roles, sessions).
choices.after: This avoids leaking data complexity into the frontend and makes the system easier to evolve or reuse.

choices.title: API-first approach
choices.mainContent: Frontend development was guided by explicit API contracts rather than implicit assumptions. Endpoints were designed around frontend needs, but kept generic enough to avoid tight coupling.
choices.after: This reduced friction during iteration and made data flow easier to reason about.

choices.title: Frontend focused on presentation and interaction
keyPoints: Consume API responses.
Handle user interactions.
Present data clearly and predictably.
choices.after: Business logic is kept out of the UI layer as much as possible, improving testability and readability.

choices.title: Pragmatic full-stack boundaries
choices.mainContent: Used Nx for monorepo management, enforcing module boundaries through library architecture and sharing TypeScript interfaces between frontend and backend.
choices.after: This architectural foundation enabled faster feature development while maintaining type safety across the full stack.

challenges.title: Keeping user state consistent
challenges.mainContent: Visitors can fill a cart before signing in. That anonymous cart had to be kept, then merged with the account's cart on login, without duplicating or losing items.
challenges.after: Making the merge rules explicit simplified the rest of the purchase flow.

challenges.title: Avoiding frontend–backend drift
challenges.mainContent: As features evolved, there was a risk of the frontend depending on backend behavior that was not explicitly defined. This was mitigated by tightening API contracts and being explicit about response shapes.
challenges.after: This discipline reduced regressions and simplified debugging.

challenges.title: Combine smooth development, security and performances
challenges.mainContent: Using an ORM as a way to reinforce security by preventing SQL injections, as well as facilitating migrations.
challenges.after: Using indexes and custom SQL requests as a way to improve performances.

keyPoints: Full-stack projects succeed or fail at the boundaries between layers.
A well-designed API simplifies everything built on top of it.
Payment and authentication flows expose design weaknesses quickly.
Clear contracts matter more than stack sophistication.
learned.after: This project reinforced the importance of thinking holistically about applications: not just how each part works, but how responsibilities are divided and communicated across the system.
